'''Efim Isaakovich Zelmanov''' ({{langx|ru|Ефи́м Исаа́кович Зе́льманов}}; born 7 September 1955) is a Russian-American<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/efim-i-zelmanov-wlvzj2/|title = Efim I. Zelmanov}}</ref> mathematician, known for his work on combinatorial problems in [[nonassociative algebra]] and [[group theory]], including his solution of the [[Burnside problem|restricted Burnside problem]]. He was awarded a [[Fields Medal]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Zürich]] in 1994.

== Biography ==

Zelmanov was born on 7 September 1955 into a [[Jew]]ish family in [[Khabarovsk]]. He entered [[Novosibirsk State University]] in 1972, when he was 17 years old.<ref>[https://faces.nsu.ru/?p=607 Interview with Zelmanov (in Russian)]</ref> He obtained a doctoral degree at [[Novosibirsk State University]] in 1980, and a higher degree at [[Leningrad State University]] in 1985. He had a position in Novosibirsk until 1987, when he left the Soviet Union.[[File:Zelmanov and Hunter in Lincoln.jpg|left|thumb|Efim Zelmanov (right) with the [[University of Lincoln]] (UK) Deputy Vice-Chancellor Professor Andrew Hunter (left) after receiving Honorary DSc degree. 5th September 2016, Lincoln, UK.]]In 1990, he moved to the [[United States]], becoming a professor at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]. He was at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1994/5, then at [[Yale University]]. In 1996, he became a Distinguished Professor at the [[Korea Institute for Advanced Study]] and in 2002, he became a professor at the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref>{{cite web|title=UCSD Press Releases: Fields Medalist Joins Mathematics Faculty at UCSD|url=http://ucsdnews.ucsd.edu/newsrel/science/mczelmanov.htm}}</ref> In 2011 he got hon DSc from QUB (Belfast)<ref>[https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/education/qub-honours-for-top-broadcaster-and-maths-genius/28634512.html QUB honours for top broadcaster and maths genius] By Lindsay Fergus, [[Belfast Telegraph]] 8 Jul 2011</ref>

In 2022, he moved to the [[People's Republic of China]] and joined the [[Southern University of Science and Technology]] in Shenzhen, China.<ref>{{cite web|title=Math master starts full-time at SUSTech|url=https://www.eyeshenzhen.com/content/2022-09/15/content_25369905.htm}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Zelmanov's Homepage at SUStech|url=https://icm.sustech.edu.cn/people/EfimZelmanov/?lang=en-us}}</ref> He served as a chair professor and the scientific director of the SUSTech International Center for Mathematics.

Zelmanov was elected a member of the [[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]] in 2001,<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200107/people.pdf National Academy of Sciences Elections], [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] '''48''' (2001), no. 7, p. 722</ref> becoming, at the age of 47, the youngest member of the mathematics section of the academy.<ref>[http://ucsdnews.ucsd.edu/archive/newsrel/science/mczelmanov.htm FIELDS MEDALIST JOINS MATHEMATICS FACULTY AT UCSD], [[University of California at San Diego]] news release,  October 28, 2002</ref> He is also an elected member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1996)<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/199607/people.pdf American Academy Elections], [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] '''43''' (1996), no. 7, p. 781</ref> and a foreign member of the [[Korean Academy of Science and Technology]] and of the [[Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences]].<ref>[http://news.ualberta.ca/newsreleases/2011/06/efimzelmanovtoreceivehonorarydoctorofsciencedegreefromuniversityofalberta Efim Zelmanov to receive honorary doctor of science degree from University of Alberta] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140422165320/http://news.ualberta.ca/newsreleases/2011/06/efimzelmanovtoreceivehonorarydoctorofsciencedegreefromuniversityofalberta |date=2014-04-22 }}, [[University of Alberta]] press release,  June 14, 2011</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-09-01.</ref>

Zelmanov gave invited talks at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Warsaw (1983), Kyoto (1990) and Zurich (1994).<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/199808/bios-all.pdf Biographies of candidates 1998], [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] '''45''' (1998), no. 8, p. 1018</ref> He delivered the 2004 Turán Memorial Lectures.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://old.renyi.hu/turanlectures_vk.html|title=Turán Memorial Lectures}}</ref> He was awarded Honorary Doctor degrees from the [[University of Hagen]], Germany (1997),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fernuni-hagen.de/mi/fakultaet/ehrenpromotionen.shtml|title=Ehrenpromotionen}}</ref> the [[University of Alberta]], Canada (2011),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ualberta.ca/news-and-events/newsarticles/2011/04/honourarydegreerecipientssettoinspire|title=Honorary degree recipients set to inspire - University of Alberta|website=www.ualberta.ca|access-date=2016-09-08|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160913214403/https://www.ualberta.ca/news-and-events/newsarticles/2011/04/honourarydegreerecipientssettoinspire|archive-date=2016-09-13}}</ref> [[Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv]], Ukraine (2012),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.univ.kiev.ua/en/geninf/hdoc/|title=Honorary Doctors|website=www.univ.kiev.ua|access-date=2016-09-08}}</ref>  the [[Universidad Internacional Menéndez Pelayo]] in Santander, Spain (2015),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lne.es/sociedad-cultura/2015/02/07/otin-zelmanov-doctores-honoris-causa/1709850.html|title=Otín y Zelmanov, doctores honoris causa por la Universidad Menéndez Pelayo|last=España|first=La Nueva|date=7 February 2015|access-date=2016-09-08}}</ref> the [[University of Lincoln]], UK (2016),<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://newsletter.lms.ac.uk/visit-of-professor-efim-zelmanov/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20160917210157/http://newsletter.lms.ac.uk/visit-of-professor-efim-zelmanov/|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 17, 2016|title=Visit of Professor Efim Zelmanov {{!}} LONDON MATHEMATICAL SOCIETY NEWSLETTER|date=July 11, 2016|website=newsletter.lms.ac.uk|access-date=2016-09-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lincoln.ac.uk/news/2016/08/1258.asp|title=Celebrating degree success as Class of 2016 graduate|last=University of Lincoln|date=31 August 2016|website=University of Lincoln Press Office|language=en|access-date=2016-09-07}}</ref> and the [[Vrije Universiteit Brussel]], Belgium (2023).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vub.be/en/news/honorary-doctorates-vub-2023|title=Honorary doctorates VUB 2023|date=1 June 2023}}</ref>

Zelmanov's early work was on [[Jordan algebra]]s in the case of infinite dimensions. He was able to show that [[Glennie's identity]] in a certain sense generates all identities that hold. He then showed that the [[Engel identity]] for [[Lie algebra]]s implies [[nilpotent Lie algebra|nilpotence]], in the case of infinite dimensions.

==Notable publications==
* Zelʹmanov, E.I. Solution of the restricted Burnside problem for groups of odd exponent. Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR Ser. Mat. 54 (1990), no. 1, 42–59, 221. English translation in Math. USSR-Izv. 36 (1991), no. 1, 41–60. [[doi:10.1070/IM1991v036n01ABEH001946]]
* Zelʹmanov, E.I. Solution of the restricted Burnside problem for 2-groups. Mat. Sb. 182 (1991), no. 4, 568–592. English translation in Math. USSR-Sb. 72 (1992), no. 2, 543–565. [[doi:10.1070/SM1992v072n02ABEH001272]]
